reference: CBA-2.C | CBA-2.C.1-2 Quality-Control Audits Audit 1 — CED Alignment and Scope All 100 questions are aligned to Topic 3.4, Learning Objective CBA-2.C: define the different types of profit, explain how firms respond to profit opportunities, and calculate a firm’s profit or loss. Coverage is limited to CBA-2.C.1 and CBA-2.C.2: firms respond to economic profit/loss rather than accounting profit; accounting profit omits implicit costs such as the cost of financial capital, compensation for risk, and an entrepreneur’s time; full compensation of these implicit costs yields normal profit. No question requires the Topic 3.5 profit-maximizing rule (MR = MC), choosing a profit-maximizing quantity, shutdown conditions, break-even rules, market entry/exit mechanics, or perfect-competition graphs. Earlier concepts such as opportunity cost are used only as prerequisites for distinguishing explicit and implicit cost. Audit 2 — Construction, Calculations, and Answer Integrity Question count: 100. Difficulty distribution: 33 Easy, 40 Medium, 27 Hard. Every item has five answer choices and exactly one keyed answer. Correct-answer positions are balanced exactly: A = 20, B = 20, C = 20, D = 20, E = 20. Every numerical item was recomputed using: accounting profit = total revenue − explicit costs; economic profit = total revenue − explicit costs − implicit costs = accounting profit − implicit costs. Zero economic profit is treated as normal profit, while negative economic profit is treated as economic loss. Distractors were constructed from common errors: omitting implicit costs, reversing accounting and economic profit, adding instead of subtracting costs, confusing forgone income with explicit payments, and interpreting positive accounting profit as necessarily positive economic profit.
